ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is a green triangle, with the base labeled 16 cm, and the right side is a vertical side; on the right side there is also a dashed right triangle connected, with the horizontal side labeled 9 cm and the hypotenuse labeled 15 cm, and this dashed triangle and the green triangle share the same vertical height. Then reason: First use the dashed right triangle to find the height, h = sqrt(15^2 - 9^2) = sqrt(225 - 81) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm. Then regard the green triangle as a right triangle whose two legs are 16 cm and 12 cm respectively, with hypotenuse sqrt(16^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(256 + 144) = sqrt(400) = 20 cm. Finally find the perimeter: 16 + 12 + 20 = 48 cm, so the perimeter of the triangle is 48.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a shaded triangle with bottom side 16 cm and a vertical right side whose length is not directly labeled. Also read the attached dashed right triangle: its horizontal leg is 9 cm, its hypotenuse is 15 cm, and it shares the same vertical height as the shaded triangle. Use the Pythagorean theorem on the dashed right triangle to find the shared height: h = sqrt(15^2 - 9^2) = 12. Then use the Pythagorean theorem again on the shaded right triangle, with legs 16 and 12, to find the slanted side: sqrt(16^2 + 12^2) = 20. Add the three shaded triangle sides: 16 + 12 + 20 = 48.
